clue.text: Today we learn outcome of not finishing Greek study class

definitions.text: Today we learn outcome of not finishing Greek study class

indicators.note: the outcome of a set of words is what they turn into, so these letters are reworked into a new order
the word Greek is cut short, losing its final letter K

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher explains that today pupils hear how their Greek class went after failing to finish the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' trims Greek to GREE; 'outcome of' then shuffles GREE + STUDY + CLASS. The whole clue also describes the day English teenagers learn their GCSE exam results; the puzzle ran on that day in August 2011.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual August day when pupils in England learn their exam grades is exactly when today brings news of how classes went.

indicators.note: a failing business falls apart, so the letters of franchisee are broken up

parts.note: these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A struggling franchise holder whose business never gets very far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' scrambles FRANCHISEE; 'doesn't get far' takes out F, A and R. '1' marks a GCSE subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese, meaning Mandarin, is a language offered as a GCSE subject.

clue.text: Poor performer may be pulled out of Derby, perhaps

definitions.text: may be pulled out of Derby, perhaps

explanation.surface: A disappointing horse withdrawn from the famous race.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is not the horse race but an American bowler hat, from which a conjurer pulls the animal. In cricket the word means a hopeless batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a weak tail-end batsman is so called, and a conjurer famously pulls one from a hat.

clue.text: Celebrities disrobe within range of flag

parts.note: celebrities are stars

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Andes is the South American mountain range
to disrobe is to strip

explanation.surface: Famous people undressing within sight of a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The national banner of the USA is known by this name for its design.

clue.text: For many, next week at work will cause a cry of dismay

definitions.text: For many, next week at work will

explanation.surface: Workers grumble about next week.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle ran just before the late-August bank holiday Monday in England, so many working weeks were one day short. The second sense is an archaic exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: An old exclamation of regret, like alas, and literally a working week missing one of its days.

explanation.surface: Enjoy a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy tomato sauce served as a dip and a lively Latin American dance share the name.

clue.text: Right away, dodgy builders overwhelmed with delight, start missing 1

indicators.note: one set of letters is swamped by the other, which surrounds it
the first letter of the synonym is lost

parts.note: delight is happiness

indicators.note: dodgy suggests unreliable, so the letters are jumbled
R, for right, is taken out of builders

explanation.surface: Shady builders thrilled, but a key thing is missing at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' drops R from builders before 'dodgy' scrambles the rest; 'start missing' removes the opening H. '1' marks the theme: a GCSE subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied business, a vocational course on commerce, was taken as a GCSE subject.

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters of point are rearranged

parts.note: Raymond Blanc is a famous French chef working in England

explanation.surface: Someone singles out the wine recommended by a celebrity chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the phrase 'point out', but it signals an anagram of POINT, giving PINOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot blanc is a white grape variety and the dry white made from it.

clue.text: Stride but don't start to run away

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped, as if it never got going

parts.note: to elope is to run away secretly to marry

explanation.surface: Advice to someone fleeing: walk briskly, but don't break into a run.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to move with long, easy strides.

clue.text: Work out how to get oxygen

explanation.surface: A fitness instruction paired with a question about breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise classes such as step are a workout, and the word literally refers to processes using air, the way cells take in oxygen.

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, as a store keeps goods

parts.note: AC, alternating current, is a mains power supply

indicators.note: only one of the two halves of the vegetable's name is kept, losing its first four letters

parts.note: kohlrabi is a turnip-shaped member of the cabbage family

explanation.surface: A grocer's supply includes half a cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' points to the theme answer, a GCSE subject. Kohlrabi is a cabbage relative, and 'half a' keeps only the second half of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic is one of the language subjects pupils can sit as a GCSE exam.

clue.text: Shop is a bit of a sideline

indicators.note: only a part of the word sideline is taken, a short run from its middle

explanation.surface: A small shop is just a minor side business.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen, shortened, is a store selling cooked meats and cheeses.

clue.text: On which one finds passenger needs air badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of needs air are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A passenger who is feeling sick and urgently needs some fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain drivers sit on the right, so the passenger is on the left, the side nearest the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK driving the kerb side of a car is where the front passenger usually sits.

clue.text: Reportedly look for ovens on beaches, maybe

indicators.note: the phrase is heard rather than read, as if passed on by word of mouth

parts.note: seek oasts: to seek is to look for, and oasts are kilns for drying hops

explanation.surface: Searching for kilns on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, a feature of Kent in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaches are one example of the shoreline where land meets ocean.

parts.note: describes the American marsupials famous for feigning death, lying rigid when threatened

explanation.surface: Animals that hold a rigid pose.
explanation.definitionFit: These marsupials play dead when attacked, going still as a corpse, hence the idiom playing possum.

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: prose is ordinary language without verse
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Recommending that a job be written up in simple terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward an idea is to propose it.

indicators.note: jumble means mix up, so the letters are thrown together

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: devil is not quite complete, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A demon made off with the items for a jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts DEVIL to DEVI; 'Jumble' shuffles THE + DEVI. A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Stole and took are synonyms, both past tenses meaning made off with.

explanation.surface: Emphasise worry.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point, and mental strain or worry.

indicators.note: the run of letters is brought out from inside the words blossom a lily

explanation.surface: A lily flowering is described as a product of a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' points to the theme: Somali is a language taken as a GCSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Somali, the language of Somalia, is a subject offered as a GCSE exam.

parts.note: amen is the congregation's response to a prayer

indicators.note: the end of dead is its final letter

explanation.surface: The right reply at a funeral when life reaches its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is the verb: to put right.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or put right a fault is to revise it.

parts.note: retro means harking back to an earlier style, so dated
to suit is to fit or be right for

explanation.surface: Altering an old-fashioned suit long after it was made.
explanation.definitionFit: To add new parts to an existing machine or building after manufacture is to upgrade it late.

indicators.note: cooking in the sense of tampering, so the letters are mixed up
the first letter of consomme is taken away

explanation.surface: A menu choice of soup, but skip the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without starter' leaves ONSOMME; 'cooking' shuffles that with CHOICE. '1' marks a GCSE subject: the school cookery and household management course.
explanation.definitionFit: Home economics, teaching cookery and household budgeting, has been taken as a GCSE subject.

clue.text: Squeeze out one suit but lead with five for 1

parts.note: to express juice is to squeeze it out
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the suit word keeps everything but its first letter, which is swapped for another at the front

parts.note: hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Instructions on wringing out a garment and leading a card suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but lead with five' replaces the H at the start of HEARTS with V, giving VEARTS. '1' marks a GCSE subject: the creative performance course.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressive arts, combining drama, dance, music and art, was a GCSE subject.

clue.text: God sees it's problematic for those following shortest route

indicators.note: problematic suggests something wrong, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Divine oversight of something troublesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveyors measuring the earth deal with geodesics, the shortest path between points on a curved surface.

explanation.surface: A description of a reserve squad.
explanation.definitionFit: A side dish accompanies a main course, and a sports team is called a side.
